parties.counterparty: SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor)

plans.note: Liability language most likely sits with the all-caps disclaimer block in Article VIX (sec-p0109/p0112/p0116); check for a consequential-damages waiver and any cap, and whether it is mutual and carves out confidentiality, IP infringement and willful misconduct. Sweep Article X and the General Provisions for a stray cap.

No article heading signals indemnity; look in Article X (confidentiality) and Article XXIV general provisions for a buried IP-infringement indemnity running from Licensor. If only a Licensee-side indemnity exists, treat as direction problem; if nothing, mark missing.

Article II license restrictions and the confidentiality/non-solicitation article are the likely homes for any covenant limiting the businesses or competing platforms Licensee may use or build; the defined 'Right of First Refusal' suggests a competition-adjacent restraint worth tracing.

Trace the defined terms 'Right of First Refusal' and 'FIELD OF USE' — these commonly carry an exclusive-dealing or first-look obligation on Licensee. Check Article II and Article VIII (commercial terms) before concluding absence.

Pricing is a fixed per-unit tier table with Supplemental Payments; an MFN burdening Licensee is unlikely. Confirm no 'best terms/most favoured' language accompanies the rate tiers before recording as absent (an MFN in our favour would not be flagged in any event).

Article X is expressly captioned 'CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION'. Check mutuality, duration, scope (employees vs. customers/introducing brokers) and whether general advertising / unsolicited applicants are carved out.

Term/termination likely rides with the 'Initial Period' definition (sec-i) and the commercial article VIII, with mechanics in General Provisions; assess whether Licensee has notice-based exit without penalty and whether Licensor can terminate at will mid-term. Notice addresses at sec-p0097/sec-575 support the delivery mechanic.

'Initial Period' is a defined term, so an auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window is probably tied to it; check the renewal notice period (target 30 days or less) and any uncapped price uplift on renewal.

General Provisions (Article XXIV) is the standard location. Confirm the chosen law is NY/DE/CA/England & Wales and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign or mandatory arbitration; note jury-waiver or forum inconvenience terms in the rationale.

Look for the assignment/successors clause in Article XXIV; confirm Licensee may assign to Affiliates and to a successor by merger without consent, and that Licensor has no termination right on our change of control. AFFILIATE is defined in Article I.

Ownership is driven by the Article I definitions (LICENSED TECHNOLOGY, DERIVATIVE WORK, INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS, MORAL RIGHTS) and the Article II grant/restrictions. Check for any assignment to Licensor of Licensee feedback, configurations, customer/trading data, or derivative works we pay for.

Article II is the grant. Test scope against the playbook: Affiliate and contractor use, FIELD OF USE limits, whether the grant is revocable at will or terminable other than for material breach, and any seat/site restrictions.

Usage/records audit rights would sit with the Article II restrictions or with the volume-based fee mechanics in Article VIII (Market Day / Supplemental Payments verification). Check frequency, notice, business-hours limits, and who bears cost.

No obvious penalty regime; check the fee article for interest on late payment, shortfall/true-up charges or stipulated damages payable by Licensee before concluding absence. Credits running to us are not flagged.

Article VIX is an express WARRANTY DISCLAIMER (merchantability, non-infringement, fitness, no assurance defects will be corrected). Likely a deviation: there appears to be no affirmative performance warranty or repair/replace/refund remedy — verify no separate warranty survives elsewhere before redlining.
No insurance heading in the outline; check General Provisions for a one-line insurance covenant. If none, record as missing given Licensor hosts the Platform and touches our trading data.

The tiered per-unit rate table (US$7.50 down to US$5.00) plus 'Market Day' and 'Supplemental Payments' definitions point to volume-based commitments; determine whether any minimum volume, monthly minimum or take-or-pay applies to Licensee and whether there is an exit.

No wind-down heading appears; check the termination consequences in Article VIII and the confidentiality return-of-materials language in Article X, which may only require Licensee to return Licensor materials. If there is no data return or migration assistance running to us, record as missing.
